page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top (CAPUT XXII.), page number 281 at top right. Main text in one column, paragraphs in roman and italic. Marginal notes in the right margin beside the text: "Visus organum," and "Visio quomodo fiat,". Catchword/signature line at the foot: "S 5" (gathering mark) and the last line "antur," at the foot of the column.

main_text.p: Actu perspicuum Medium est, quo proprius cujusq; rei color perspicitur, & sine lumine nullus omnino color videri potest.
Perspicua & radiis pervia sunt aër & aqua, item quædam composita, ut vitrum, tenue cornu, Crystallus.

Organum visus exterius est Oculus, seu pupilla binorum oculorum, qui sunt tanquam speculatores in suprema corporis arce collocati rotundi, ut capiendæ quantitati sufficerent, & celerius visu apprehendere valeant multa. Visus organum.
Interius est Nervus opticus & Spiritus animalis.

Fit autem visio non emittendo, sed specie visibili extrinsecus in oculum receptâ, & inde beneficio Spiritus animalis per nervos opticos in pupillam oculi deducti, ad cerebrum, ubi sensus communis est, delata. Visio quomodo fiat.

Cujus receptionis modus talis est: Primùm à corporibus aspectabilibus manant species quædam in circumfusum aërem, luce solis vel ignis illustratum, ipsumque afficiunt & in eo semper hærent: & tam longè sese, nisi ab interveniente quodam corpore opaco impedi-antur,

page.notes: Marginal notes read "Visus organum," (beside the Oculus paragraph) and "Visio quomodo fiat," (beside the paragraph on reception of vision). The last line is cut at the foot; "antur," is the end of the word "impediantur" split across the page. The page number 281 is at the top right. Text is set in a roman face with italic terms; "Medium" and "Perspicua" are in italic. Some letters such as "Criftallus" read as printed (long s form rendered as s). Ligatures in "Spiritus animalis" and the catchword area at the foot were not clearly legible; the foot line reads only "S 5".
